The proposed method relies heavily on external object detection (Cascade Mask R-CNN), whereas the primary baselines it is compared against (HA-DPO, HACL, Woodpecker) do not use such auxiliary information. This makes the "state-of-the-art" claim misleading; the improvement is largely driven by the *input* of ground-truth-adjacent detection data rather than the tuning mechanism itself. The fair baseline (Hard Prompt, which also uses detection) shows only marginal gains on stronger models (e.g., +0.27% on LLaVA-v1.5), suggesting the method's value is specific to rescuing poorly aligned models rather than a universal fix.

The evidence provided (a probing experiment with a detection head) is suggestive but not causal, yet the authors frame it as a definitive identification of the root cause. Additionally, the effectiveness of PATCH is **entirely dependent on the quality of the external detector; if the detector fails (false positives/negatives), the performance likely collapses. The paper lacks any analysis of detector robustness, which is a critical practical concern. The reliance on external, latency-heavy components also warrants a discussion on inference efficiency, which is missing.
